About The Role

The GIS Analyst is responsible for the development, maintenance, and quality control of geospatial data and mapping products in support of high-voltage transmission line and right-of-way (ROW) construction projects. This role serves as a core contributor across project lifecycle phases – from preconstruction survey coordination through as-built deliverable production.

Company Overview

Established in 1891, The L.E. Myers Co. (L.E. Myers) – the oldest MYR Group Inc. subsidiary – is recognized as a premier electrical contractor of large utility construction projects across the nation. We are proud to offer our employees the opportunity to complete training, projects, and collaborative learning alongside our family of subsidiaries. We offer stability, with long-term clients and continuous expansion, which allows our tenured employees and new team members space to grow.

At L.E. Myers, we provide structured and strategic occupational growth opportunities for our valued staff. Comprised of long- and short-tenured employees, we are interactive amongst our growing family of subsidiaries, which allows employees to participate in clean energy projects, as well as complete our long-time transmission and distribution projects

Essential Functions

Geospatial Data Management & Mapping
Develop and maintain GIS maps and databases for transmission line construction projects, including structure locations, ROW boundaries, access routes, environmental constraints, and project layers in ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Online; continuously update and manage data to support field operations and ensure teams have access to current, reliable information
Produce high-quality maps, exhibits, and spatial deliverables for internal and external project teams
Perform spatial analysis including buffer analysis, route comparisons, conflict identification, and land ownership overlays
Manage and QA/QC geospatial data from multiple sources including survey, LiDAR, aerial imagery, and CAD conversion

Transmission Line & ROW Support
Support permitting teams with accurate construction-specific mapping designs
Coordinate with survey and engineering teams to integrate field data into GIS deliverables and ensure alignment with project design drawings
Update GIS records to reflect field changes and design revisions throughout construction.
Assist with as-built documentation and final record mapping for transmission line projects

Field & Cross-Functional Coordination
Maintain internal GIS users, including onboarding new users, managing permissions, and coordinating ArcGIS Online (AGO) map sharing to ensure appropriate access, data security, and consistent use across project teams
Utilize ArcGIS Field Maps for data collection, field verification, and real-time updates during active construction
Collaborate with Project Managers, ROW agents, Environmental staff, and Survey crews to ensure GIS deliverables meet project milestones
Communicate with client GIS teams to align data standards, projections, and file format requirements

Essential functions of this position are to be performed in a Company-designated office or field location
Regular and predictable attendance
Other duties as assigned
Understand and comply with the Company's Code of Business Conduct and Ethics and other industry-specific professional and ethical conduct standards

Qualifications

Minimum of 3 years of GIS experience with a focus on utility, transmission, or linear infrastructure projects
Experience with coordinate systems, projections, and datum transformations
PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:
Experience working for an EPC contractor, transmission contractor, or utility in a GIS capacity
Familiarity with ArcGIS Online, and/or ArcGIS Field Maps for field data collection
GISP certification or ESRI Technical Certification
CAD experience (AutoCAD Civil 3D or MicroStation) for cross-functional data exchange

Preferred Education

Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Geography, Geomatics, Civil Engineering Technology, or a related field; combination of relevant education and experience considered in lieu of degree

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Proficiency in ArcGIS Pro and/or ArcGIS Online (Esri platform)
Proficiency with geodatabases, feature classes, and geoprocessing tools
Working knowledge of transmission line construction processes, ROW fundamentals, and land ownership data
Ability to read and interpret survey plats, legal descriptions, construction drawings, and one-line diagrams
Strong attention to data accuracy and QA/QC discipline
Knowledge of NERC/FERC transmission standards, NESC structure classifications, or utility asset management frameworks is preferred
Proficiency in MS Office Suite
Strong communication skills, verbal and written
Ability to travel 25%

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is adding experienced Cost Estimators to our Disaster Recovery team to support current and future disaster recovery operations across the United States.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world's most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential - join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.
Support development of FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF) analyses when required.
Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in construction estimating, engineering, architecture, construction management, infrastructure planning, or a related discipline.
Experience developing conceptual, parametric, and detailed cost estimates for infrastructure or facility projects.
Experience estimating labor, equipment, material, and construction costs.
Familiarity with modern construction practices, facility assessments, project scope development, and construction inspection activities.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for field assignments.
Valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance regulations, policy, eligibility requirements, and the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG).
Previous FEMA experience as a Cost Estimator, Program Delivery Manager, Site Inspector, Hazard Mitigation Specialist, Policy Advisor, or similar disaster recovery role.
Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Physical Requirements

Ability to perform field inspections and site visits at disaster-impacted facilities and infrastructure when required by an assignment.
Ability to travel to client offices, applicant facilities, disaster recovery operation centers, and other project locations as needed.
Ability to perform computer-based estimating and technical review activities for extended periods during remote or office-based assignments.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Work assignments may be performed remotely, in the field, or through a hybrid arrangement depending on client needs and project requirements.
Field assignments may take place in disaster-impacted communities and at damaged public facilities or infrastructure sites.
Work conditions and location may vary by assignment, including active disaster recovery operations and geographically dispersed project teams.

Additional Information

This is an on-call, as-needed cadre position. Work assignments are not guaranteed and depend on disaster declarations, contract awards, client needs, project requirements, qualifications, availability, and recovery program activations.
Acceptance of assignments is voluntary, and periods of inactivity between deployments may occur.
Assignment schedules may be flexible and may include periods of high-intensity workload during active recovery operations.
Some deployments may require extended travel or mobilization on short notice; other assignments may be fully remote.
Evening and weekend work may be required during surge events or active disaster recovery operations.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.

Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in construction estimating, engineering, architecture, construction management, infrastructure planning, or a related discipline.
Experience developing conceptual, parametric, and detailed cost estimates for infrastructure or facility projects.
Experience estimating labor, equipment, material, and construction costs.
Familiarity with modern construction practices, facility assessments, project scope development, and construction inspection activities.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for field assignments.
Valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.

Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Ability to perform computer-based estimating and technical review activities for extended periods during remote or office-based assignments.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Work assignments may be performed remotely, in the field, or through a hybrid arrangement depending on client needs and project requirements.

Work conditions and location may vary by assignment, including active disaster recovery operations and geographically dispersed project teams.

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

Position Summary

As a Cost Estimator in Tetra Tech's Disaster Recovery Cadre, you will support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs by developing accurate, defensible, and well-documented cost estimates for infrastructure restoration, emergency work, and permanent work projects. You will evaluate damaged infrastructure, develop and validate project scopes, prepare cost estimates, and support funding eligibility determinations for public facilities and infrastructure.

This is an on-call, as-needed position supporting disaster recovery programs following hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, and other federally declared disasters. Assignments may be remote, field-based, or hybrid depending on client needs and project requirements.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions:

Project Scoping and Damage Assessment

Support FEMA Public Assistance and other disaster recovery programs through project scoping, damage assessment, and cost estimating activities.
Support site inspections of damaged facilities and infrastructure to understand disaster-related damages, proposed repairs, and construction requirements.
Evaluate project scope, means and methods of construction, and restoration approaches.
Assist with the development and validation of disaster recovery project scopes.
Collaborate with applicants, engineers, architects, contractors, and program staff to define eligible work and project requirements.

Cost Estimating

Prepare conceptual, parametric, and detailed bottom-up cost estimates for disaster recovery projects.
Develop labor, equipment, materials, subcontractor, and general conditions cost estimates.
Estimate costs associated with repair, restoration, reconstruction, mitigation, and replacement projects.
Prepare cost analyses for roads, bridges, utilities, buildings, drainage systems, parks, and other public infrastructure.
Support development of FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF) analyses when required.
Develop estimate documentation that is clear, defensible, and suitable for audit and program review purposes.

Technical Review and Compliance

Review engineering reports, plans, specifications, contractor proposals, and construction cost documentation.
Evaluate project assumptions, quantities, unit costs, and estimating methodologies.
Apply knowledge of applicable construction standards, codes, and regulatory requirements.
Identify cost drivers, scope changes, and factors impacting project eligibility and funding.
Assist project teams with cost validation, reasonableness determinations, and documentation reviews.

Program Delivery Support

Provide technical estimating expertise to project managers, Public Assistance consultants, and applicant representatives.
Participate in project formulation meetings and recovery planning discussions.
Support Requests for Information (RFIs), technical reviews, appeals support, and other recovery program activities.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, architects, environmental specialists, grant professionals, and construction experts.
Maintain project records and supporting documentation in accordance with client and program requirements.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in construction estimating, engineering, architecture, construction management, infrastructure planning, or a related discipline.
Experience developing conceptual, parametric, and detailed cost estimates for infrastructure or facility projects.
Experience estimating labor, equipment, material, and construction costs.
Familiarity with modern construction practices, facility assessments, project scope development, and construction inspection activities.
Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication abilities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
Ability to work independently and effectively under changing priorities and demanding schedules.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for field assignments.
Valid driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Infrastructure Management, or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE), Registered Architect (RA), Licensed Contractor, Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Cost Estimator, or similar professional credential.
Experience using RSMeans, Xactimate, FEMA Cost Estimating Format (CEF), or other industry-standard estimating platforms.
Knowledge of FEMA Public Assistance regulations, policy, eligibility requirements, and the Public Assistance Program and Policy Guide (PAPPG).
Previous FEMA experience as a Cost Estimator, Program Delivery Manager, Site Inspector, Hazard Mitigation Specialist, Policy Advisor, or similar disaster recovery role.
Experience with roads, utilities, drainage systems, site development, vertical construction, or public infrastructure projects.
Experience supporting disaster recovery, grant-funded infrastructure programs, or public sector capital projects.

Physical Requirements

Ability to perform field inspections and site visits at disaster-impacted facilities and infrastructure when required by an assignment.
Ability to travel to client offices, applicant facilities, disaster recovery operation centers, and other project locations as needed.
Ability to perform computer-based estimating and technical review activities for extended periods during remote or office-based assignments.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

Work assignments may be performed remotely, in the field, or through a hybrid arrangement depending on client needs and project requirements.
Field assignments may take place in disaster-impacted communities and at damaged public facilities or infrastructure sites.
Work conditions and location may vary by assignment, including active disaster recovery operations and geographically dispersed project teams.

Additional Information

This is an on-call, as-needed cadre position. Work assignments are not guaranteed and depend on disaster declarations, contract awards, client needs, project requirements, qualifications, availability, and recovery program activations.
Acceptance of assignments is voluntary, and periods of inactivity between deployments may occur.
Assignment schedules may be flexible and may include periods of high-intensity workload during active recovery operations.
Some deployments may require extended travel or mobilization on short notice; other assignments may be fully remote.
Evening and weekend work may be required during surge events or active disaster recovery operations.

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

You are a seasoned project coordinator with experience in the interior design and/or furniture industry. You’re organized and borderline obsessed with your checklists. You’re an excellent communicator - direct, honest, kind, dependable, and takes and gives feedback well. You have a low ego and are willing to jump in to help others. An outstanding collaborator and team player, you value your fellow team members and enthusiastically contribute to AP’s culture of leading with kindness and accountability. Enter and maintain project specifications within procurement software.
Audit furniture floor plans and review FF&E specifications for accuracy and completeness.

Track and expedite submittals, prototypes, production schedules, in-production items, and delivery timelines to ensure all products arrive at the warehouse according to schedule.

Conduct final walkthroughs with clients and designers to confirm project completion.
Develop and issue punch lists to Project Managers and clients, and coordinate with the Project Manager to resolve outstanding items.
Compile project closeout documentation and reconcile final payments against the approved project budget.
Attend weekly team meetings to review project progress and identify opportunities to support Project Managers as needed.

2–3 years of experience in purchasing, procurement, project coordination, or a related field.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Google Workspace applications.
Strong attention to detail while maintaining the ability to understand the broader project scope and priorities.
Excellent customer service skills with exceptional verbal and written communication across in-person, phone, and digital platforms.
Demonstrated ability to manage time effectively in a remote work environment, balancing multiple projects, deadlines, and priorities.
Ability to read and interpret FF&E specifications, shop drawings, and interior design documents, including furniture plans, floor finish plans, reflected ceiling plans, and elevations.
Proactive problem-solving skills with the ability to anticipate issues and support efficient resolution.
Adaptability and resourcefulness, with the ability to remain effective in fast-paced or evolving project environments.
Strong collaboration skills, including clear and proactive communication with team members, clients, designers, contractors, and installation teams.
Open to constructive feedback and committed to continuous learning and professional growth.
Positive, team-oriented mindset with the ability to work collaboratively and maintain focus through project deadlines and completion.
Ability to support and coordinate furniture installations, including working on active construction sites and engaging with project stakeholders such as general contractors and installers.
Comfortable working in job-site environments, including unfinished spaces, and performing physical tasks such as bending, kneeling, climbing, and lifting up to 25 pounds.
Availability to work full-time during regular business hours, with occasional overtime or weekend travel as project needs require.
